definitions.explanation: Describes hair, grass, or vegetation that has grown wild and uncontrolled.
The sound or manner of flames burning intensely.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→にわ：02239_niwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{草|くさ}→くさ：02206_kusa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{生|は}えている→はえる：02392_haeru⟧。
examples.english: The grass in the garden has grown wild.

examples.japanese: ⟦{留守|るす}→るす：01754_rusu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間|あいだ}→あいだ：00914_aida⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{庭|にわ}→にわ：02239_niwa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦しまった→しまう：03064_shimau⟧。
examples.english: While I was away, the garden became completely overgrown.

examples.japanese: ⟦{火|ひ}→ひ：02248_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう⟦{燃|も}えている→もえる：02312_moeru⟧。
⟦{山火事|やまかじ}→やまかじ：19433_yamakaji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{燃|も}え→もえる：02312_moeru⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がった→ひろがる：01980_hirogaru⟧。

⟦{焚|た}き{火|び}→たきび：06992_takibi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{音|おと}→おと：00743_oto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てて→たてる：01196_tateru⟧⟦{燃|も}えていて→もえる：02312_moeru⟧、⟦{夜|よる}→よる：00487_yoru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{森|もり}→もり：02260_mori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{明|あか}るく→あかるい：00616_akarui⟧⟦{照|て}らしていた→てらす：04669_terasu⟧。
examples.english: The bonfire blazed with a roar, brightly illuminating the nighttime forest.

notes:
An onomatopoeic word with two distinct senses. Can be used as an adverb (often with ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧) or as a na-adjective.

SENSE 1 (OVERGROWN):
Describes vegetation or hair that has grown wild and untidy.
- ⟦{草|くさ}→くさ：02206_kusa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう: grass has grown wild
- ⟦{髭|ひげ}→ひげ：01332_hige⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう: unkempt beard
- ⟦{髪|かみ}→かみ：02196_kami⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう: disheveled hair
- ぼうぼう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{生|は}える→はえる：02392_haeru⟧: to grow wild

SENSE 2 (BLAZING):
Describes the sound and manner of fire burning fiercely.
- ⟦{火|ひ}→ひ：02248_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ぼうぼう⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{燃|も}える→もえる：02312_moeru⟧: fire blazes fiercely

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ぼさぼさ→ぼさぼさ：noentry⟧: messy, disheveled (hair — less extreme)
- ⟦めらめら→めらめら：05375_meramera⟧: flames flickering/licking
- ⟦ごうごう→ごうごう：22356_gougou⟧: roaring (fire, wind, water — louder)

USAGE:
The overgrown sense implies neglect — things have been left unattended.
